en: to look older; to look premature

examples.en: That friend looks older than their age.

examples.ko: 요즘 잠을 못 자서 겉늙은 것 같아요.
examples.en: I haven't been sleeping lately, so I feel like I look older than I am.
He looks prematurely old; he's thirty but looks forty.
My mother worried a lot and aged early in appearance.

examples.ko: 어른스러운 옷만 입으면 겉늙게 보일 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you only wear grown-up clothes, you may look older than you are.

examples.ko: 겉늙었다는 말을 들었지만 속은 아이 같아요.
examples.en: I was told I look older than I am, but inside I'm like a kid.

explain: 실제 나이보다 겉모습이 늙어 보일 때 써요. 반대로 어려 보이는 얼굴은 '동안이다'라고 해요. 사람 앞에서 쓰면 기분이 상할 수 있으니 조심해서 말해요.

phrases.en: With a beard, you look older than you are.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다는 뜻으로 '-아/어 보이다'와 자주 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used with -아/어 보이다 to mean someone looks that way.
phrases.en_equiv: to look older than one is

phrases.en: I'm tired, so my face looks older than it should.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form used to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: For his age, he looks much older.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 그렇게 된 상태를 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the past form for a state that has already happened.

explain_en: It is used when someone's appearance looks older than their real age. The opposite, a youthful face, is '동안이다'. It can hurt someone's feelings if said to them, so be careful.

en: to scrumple

examples.en: These clothes got all wrinkled after I put them in the bag.
I smoothed out the wrinkled shirt with an iron.

examples.ko: 종이가 구깃구깃해서 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The paper is so crumpled that I can't read the writing well.
The handkerchief was folded in a crumpled way.

examples.ko: 옷이 구깃구깃하면 면접에서 인상이 안 좋을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If your clothes are wrinkled, you may make a bad impression at an interview.

examples.ko: 구깃구깃하지 않은 옷을 입고 나가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to go out in clothes that aren't wrinkled.

explain: '구기다'는 누가 구기는 동작이고, '구겨지다'는 구겨지는 변화예요. '구깃구깃하다'는 이미 여기저기 구겨진 상태를 묘사해요. 보통 '구깃구깃한 옷'처럼 뒤에 명사를 꾸며요.

phrases.en: The book got wet in the rain and became crumpled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구겨지지 않았다가 구겨진 상태로 변하는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for changing from smooth to crumpled.

phrases.en: I ironed it, so the shirt isn't wrinkled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이에요. 깨끗하게 펴진 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for something nicely smooth.

phrases.en: I smoothed out the crumpled paper and read it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 구겨진 상태의 물건을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe something that is already crumpled.

explain_en: '구기다' is the action of crumpling and '구겨지다' is the change of becoming crumpled. '구깃구깃하다' describes the state of already being wrinkled in many places. It usually modifies a noun, as in '구깃구깃한 옷'.

en: to be itchy; to be scratchy

examples.en: The spot where a mosquito bit me is itchy.
My back is itchy but I can't reach it.

examples.ko: 새 옷의 털 때문에 목이 근지러웠어요.
examples.en: My neck felt itchy because of the fuzz on the new clothes.
It itched so I scratched it, and it got even redder.
If your body feels itchy, go see a doctor.
My eyes are itchy and my nose is stuffed up.

explain: ㅂ 불규칙이라서 '근지러워요', '근지러운', '근지러웠어요'로 바뀌어요. '간지럽다'는 누가 건드려서 웃음이 날 것 같은 느낌이고, '근지럽다'는 '가렵다'처럼 긁고 싶은 느낌이라 서로 달라요.

phrases.en: The place where the mosquito bit me is so itchy.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㅂ 불규칙 활용의 해요체로, 일상 대화에서 가장 기본으로 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite 해요체 form with the ㅂ irregular change, the basic form in daily talk.

phrases.en: I put ointment on the itchy spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형으로, 몸의 어느 부분인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form before a noun, used to point to a part of the body.

phrases.en: I put medicine on, so it's not itchy anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이라서 ㅂ이 바뀌지 않고 '근지럽지'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative form the ㅂ does not change, so it stays 근지럽지.

explain_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '근지러워요', '근지러운' and '근지러웠어요'. '간지럽다' is the ticklish feeling that makes you want to laugh when touched, whereas '근지럽다' is an itch you want to scratch, like '가렵다', so they differ.

en: to scratch

examples.en: He scratched his head as if he were embarrassed.

examples.ko: 모기에 물린 팔을 계속 긁적거리지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't keep scratching the arm where the mosquito bit you.

examples.ko: 질문을 받자 선생님은 뒷목을 긁적거리며 웃었어요.
examples.en: When asked the question, the teacher laughed while scratching the back of his neck.
The child was scratching his nose, so I asked if it itched.
Why do you keep scratching your chin?

examples.ko: 시험지를 보며 머리를 긁적거리는 학생이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many students were scratching their heads as they looked at the test paper.

explain: '긁다'보다 손끝으로 가볍게 여러 번 긁는 느낌이에요. 가려울 때뿐 아니라 쑥스럽거나 난처할 때 머리를 긁는 행동에도 자주 써요. '긁적이다'도 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: He was embarrassed and just scratched his head.
phrases.nuance_ko: '긁적거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 짧아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 긁적거리다, a little shorter.

phrases.en: When I got a question I didn't know, I scratched my head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 난처하거나 쑥스러울 때 하는 행동으로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for the gesture made when puzzled or shy.

phrases.en: Please don't keep scratching the wound.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 마세요'를 붙이면 하지 말라는 부탁을 공손하게 할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -지 마세요 makes a polite request not to do it.

explain_en: Compared with '긁다', it feels like lightly scratching several times with the fingertips. It is used not only for itching but also for scratching your head when you feel shy or awkward. '긁적이다' is used in a similar way.

en: to be grubby; to be filthy; to be squalid

examples.en: I haven't washed it for days, so the clothes are grubby.
Don't go out wearing those filthy sneakers.
The room is grimy, so I need to clean it.
After playing at the playground, the child's face was grubby.
Your hair looks grubby, so go wash it.
If you don't wash, you'll get grubby quickly.

explain: '더럽다'보다 오래 씻거나 빨지 않아 때가 타서 꾀죄죄한 느낌이에요. 뜻이 비슷한 '꾀죄죄하다'도 있어요. 부사 '꼬질꼬질'과 짝으로 외워 두세요.

phrases.en: The old doll looks grubby.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'로 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 보이다' says that something looks that way.

phrases.en: I didn't wash my face, so it looks scruffy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷한 말로, 지저분하고 초라한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word with a dirty, shabby feel.

phrases.en: The sneakers were just washed, so they aren't grubby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨끗한 상태를 부정형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say something is clean.

explain_en: Compared with '더럽다', it has the feel of being shabby and grimy from not being washed for a long time. '꾀죄죄하다' is a similar word. It pairs well with the adverb '꼬질꼬질'.

en: to be grubby; to be filthy

examples.en: His face looks grubby, as if he hasn't washed for days.
That child looked shabby and grimy in his clothes.
I washed my grubby sneakers and made them look new.
The room is so grubby, so let's clean first.

examples.ko: 밤새 일하고 나서 꾀죄죄한 모습으로 집에 왔어요.
examples.en: After working all night, I came home looking scruffy.
The towels got grimy, so I bought new ones.

explain: 사람의 모습이나 옷, 물건이 때가 타고 초라해 보일 때 써요. 그냥 '더럽다'보다 낡고 후줄근한 느낌이 있어요. 사람에게 직접 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I don't want to go out wearing grubby clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 옷이나 물건을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -ㄴ it describes clothes or objects.

phrases.en: I didn't wash my hair, so I look grubby.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'로 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -아/어 보이다 says it looks that way on the outside.

phrases.en: It's old but clean, so it doesn't look grubby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡았어도 깔끔하다는 말을 할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says something is tidy even if it's old.

explain_en: It describes a person, clothes or things that look dirty and shabby. Compared with plain '더럽다', it has a worn-out, scruffy feel. Saying it directly to a person can be rude.

en: nylon

examples.en: These socks are made of nylon, so they are durable.
Nylon clothes dry fast, so they are convenient.
I tied the tent with a nylon rope.
Nylon shirts are a bit hot in summer.
Fishing line is usually nylon.
It is a nylon bag, so it is fine even in the rain.

explain: '면'은 식물, '울'은 양털에서 얻고 나일론은 공장에서 만든 섬유라서 가볍고 빨리 말라요. 한국에서는 '나일론 양말', '나일론 줄'처럼 옷감이나 재료 이름 앞에 붙여 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Nylon socks are good because they dry quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나일론' 뒤에 물건 이름을 붙여 옷감이 나일론이라는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an item name after 'nylon' to say it is made of nylon.

phrases.en: I tied up the bag with nylon rope.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷감뿐 아니라 줄 같은 재료에도 '나일론'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Nylon' is used for materials like rope, not just clothes.

phrases.en: This bag is made of nylon, so it is light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 만든 재료를 말할 때 '소재'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'material' to describe what something is made of.

explain_en: '면' comes from plants and '울' from sheep, while 나일론 is a factory-made fiber that is light and dries quickly. In Korean it often comes before the item, as in '나일론 양말' and '나일론 줄'.

en: rags; tatters

examples.ko: 할머니는 누더기가 된 옷을 꿰매서 다시 입으셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother mended the tattered clothes and wore them again.
The old blanket has worn out into rags.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 누더기를 걸치고도 환하게 웃었어요.
examples.en: The child smiled brightly even while wearing rags.

examples.ko: 이 신발은 이제 누더기 같아서 버려야 해요.
examples.en: These shoes look like rags now, so I have to throw them away.
After so many changes, the plan has turned into a patchwork mess.

examples.ko: 그 법은 고치고 또 고쳐서 누더기라는 말까지 들어요.
examples.en: That law has been amended so many times that people even call it a patchwork.

explain: 옷뿐 아니라 계획, 법, 글처럼 여러 번 고쳐서 엉망이 된 것을 비유할 때도 써요. '넝마'와 비슷하게 쓰지만 '누더기'는 기운 자국이 많은 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 법을 계속 덧붙여 고쳤더니 누더기가 됐다는 말이 나와요.
phrases.en: to become a patchwork mess
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이나 법, 글을 여러 번 고쳐서 처음 모습이 사라지고 엉망이 됐다는 비판의 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A critical way to say something was revised so many times that it lost its original shape and became a mess.

explain_en: Besides clothes, it is also used figuratively for plans, laws or writing that have been revised so many times they became a mess. It is similar to '넝마', but '누더기' has a stronger feel of being full of patches.

en: to be bushy

examples.en: My hair is shaggy, so I need to go to the hair salon.
He showed up with a bushy beard.
My older brother, whom I hadn't seen in a while, had shaggy hair.
I want to tidy up my shaggy bangs.
My eyebrows grew bushy, so I trimmed them.
The puppy's fur is too shaggy.

explain: 머리카락, 수염, 털이 길고 많이 나서 정리가 안 된 모습에 써요. 단정하지 않다는 느낌이 있어서 '머리가 덥수룩해요'는 이발할 때가 됐다는 말로도 들려요. '텁수룩하다'도 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I feel refreshed after cutting my shaggy hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: I've been busy lately, so my beard is bushy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금의 모습을 해요체로 말하는 가장 기본 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic polite form for describing how it looks now.

phrases.en: My hair is shaggy, so I need to tidy it up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같은 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A near-synonym with almost the same meaning.

explain_en: It describes hair, beard or fur that is long, thick and untidy. It carries a feeling of looking unkempt, so '머리가 덥수룩해요' hints that a haircut is due. '텁수룩하다' is used in a similar way.

en: uniform

examples.en: I went to class wearing my taekwondo uniform.
The belt color on my uniform is blue now.

examples.ko: 아들이 도복 입은 모습이 정말 멋있어요.
examples.en: My son looks really cool in his uniform.
I washed the uniform and hung it out on the balcony.
A judo uniform is thick, so it's hot in summer.

examples.ko: 도복 가방을 안 가져와서 다시 집에 갔어요.
examples.en: I forgot my uniform bag, so I went back home.

explain: 태권도, 유도, 검도처럼 무술을 할 때 입는 옷이에요. '태권도복, 유도복'처럼 종목 이름을 앞에 붙여 말하기도 해요. 태권도와 유도 도복은 허리에 띠를 매고, 띠 색깔로 실력 단계를 나타내요.

phrases.en: My taekwondo uniform got small, so I bought a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종목 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 운동 옷인지 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the sport first makes clear which uniform it is.

phrases.en: A judo uniform is thick and sturdy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유도할 때 입는 도복을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The uniform worn for judo.

phrases.en: We wear the uniform during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동하러 갈 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for going to practice.
phrases.en_equiv: to wear a martial arts uniform

explain_en: It is the clothing worn for martial arts such as taekwondo, judo and kendo. People also put the sport in front, as in '태권도복' and '유도복'. Taekwondo and judo uniforms are worn with a belt at the waist, and the belt color shows the level.

en: to be dumpy; to be chunky

examples.en: That man is short and stocky.
He has a short, stout build, but he is really strong.
The teddy bear is cuter because it is short and chubby.
A short, chubby puppy is waddling along.

examples.ko: 이 컵은 땅딸막하고 두툼해서 손에 잘 잡혀요.
examples.en: This cup is short and thick, so it is easy to hold.
He may look short and stocky, but he runs really fast.

explain: 키가 작고 몸이 퉁퉁하거나 옆으로 넓어 보이는 모습이라 '날씬하다'와는 반대쪽이에요. 사람의 몸에 직접 쓰면 외모 평가가 되어 실례일 수 있어요. 컵이나 병 같은 물건에는 부담 없이 쓰고, '땅딸하다'는 조금 짧게 줄인 말이에요.

phrases.en: It's a short, chunky cup, so it fits snugly in my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건에 쓰면 귀엽다는 느낌이라 부담이 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used on objects it sounds cute and carries no offense.

phrases.example: 이 화분은 땅딸막해 보여도 안정감이 있어요.
phrases.en: This flowerpot looks squat, but it feels stable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습의 인상을 말할 때 '-해 보이다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-해 보이다' describes the impression from appearance.

phrases.en: The squat bottle doesn't fit on the shelf.
phrases.nuance_ko: '땅딸막하다'를 줄인 말로 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 땅딸막하다 with the same meaning.

explain_en: It describes a short, wide, plump shape, the opposite of '날씬하다' (slim). Using it directly about a person's body is a comment on their looks and can be rude. It is fine for objects like cups and bottles, and '땅딸하다' is a slightly shorter form.

en: to be neat; to be clean

examples.en: It was an interview, so I went dressed neatly.

examples.ko: 아버지는 양복을 입으면 늘 말쑥해 보이세요.
examples.en: My father always looks neat and sharp in a suit.
A neatly dressed young man asked me for directions.

examples.ko: 머리를 자르고 나니 얼굴이 훨씬 말쑥해요.
examples.en: After the haircut, your face looks much cleaner.
His clean and tidy appearance was impressive.

examples.ko: 말쑥하던 사람이 오늘은 왜 이렇게 지저분해요?
examples.en: He is usually so neat, so why is he so messy today?

explain: 차림새나 얼굴이 깨끗하고 단정할 때 잘 어울려요. '깔끔하다'는 방, 음식, 성격에도 두루 쓰지만 말쑥하다는 사람의 겉모습에 더 많이 써요. 글이나 격식 있는 자리에서 어울리는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I went to the wedding looking neat and clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔서 옷차림이 깨끗하고 단정하다고 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form, used to describe a clean, tidy outfit.

phrases.en: It was a blind date, so I dressed up neatly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 자리에 단정하게 옷을 갖춰 입을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when dressing up neatly for an important occasion.

phrases.en: That student's clothes are always tidy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말쑥하다'와 비슷하지만 옷차림뿐 아니라 태도나 몸가짐에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '말쑥하다', but also used for manners and behavior, not just clothing.

explain_en: It fits best when a person's outfit or face looks clean and tidy. '깔끔하다' is used widely for rooms, food and personality, but '말쑥하다' is used more for a person's appearance. It has a somewhat written or formal feel.

en: to trim; to touch; to tidy up

examples.en: I tidied my hair in front of the mirror and went out.
Mom straightened the child's collar for him.
Before the interview, I smoothed out my outfit.
He stroked his beard, lost in thought.

examples.ko: 글을 한 번 더 매만지면 훨씬 좋아질 거예요.
examples.en: If you polish the writing once more, it will get much better.
I arranged the flowers nicely and put them in a vase.

explain: 머리, 옷, 얼굴처럼 몸을 단정하게 다듬을 때 자주 써요. 글을 고치고 다듬는 뜻으로도 쓰여서 '손보다'와 비슷해요. 그냥 '만지다'보다 부드럽게 정리하는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I straightened my clothes before going into the interview.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구겨진 곳을 펴고 단정하게 정리한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means smoothing out wrinkles and tidying up clothes.

phrases.example: 밤새 쓴 글을 아침에 한 번 더 매만졌어요.
phrases.en: I polished the writing I wrote overnight once more in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 쓴 글을 조금씩 고치고 다듬을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for refining a piece of writing bit by bit.

phrases.example: 언니가 제 머리를 예쁘게 매만져 줬어요.
phrases.en: My sister styled my hair nicely for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 위해 다듬어 주는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when tidying something up for another person.

explain_en: It is often used for neatening things like hair, clothes, or face. It can also mean polishing writing, similar to '손보다'. It feels softer and more careful than plain '만지다'.

en: hair texture; condition of one's hair

examples.en: After I changed shampoo, my hair became softer.

examples.ko: 드라이를 너무 자주 하면 머릿결에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Blow-drying too often is bad for your hair.
My sister's hair shines like silk.
I rinse with cold water to protect my hair.

examples.ko: 염색을 자주 했더니 머릿결 상태가 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: Since I dyed my hair often, its condition got worse.

examples.ko: 요즘은 머릿결까지 신경 쓰는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days many people care even about the texture of their hair.

explain: 머릿결은 머리카락의 윤기와 부드러운 정도를 말해요. '머릿결이 좋다', '머릿결이 상하다', '머릿결이 푸석푸석하다'처럼 써요. 머리 모양은 '생머리', '곱슬머리'로 따로 말해요.

phrases.en: My older sister has good hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리카락이 윤기 나고 부드럽다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment that hair is shiny and soft.

phrases.en: My hair got damaged from dyeing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리카락이 거칠어지고 나빠졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means hair has become rough and damaged.

phrases.en: My hair gets dry and rough in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윤기 없이 마른 머리카락을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes dry, dull hair.

explain_en: 머릿결 describes how shiny and soft your hair is. People say 머릿결이 좋다, 머릿결이 상하다, or 머릿결이 푸석푸석하다. Hair shape is described separately with words like 생머리 and 곱슬머리.

en: to feel sick; to feel like throwing up

examples.en: After riding the boat, my stomach feels queasy.

examples.ko: 차 안에서 책을 읽었더니 속이 메슥메슥했어요.
examples.en: I read a book in the car and felt nauseous.
I felt sick and dizzy since morning, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 기름진 음식 냄새를 맡으면 속이 메슥메슥해져요.
examples.en: When I smell greasy food, my stomach starts to feel queasy.

examples.ko: 속이 메슥메슥할 때는 따뜻한 물을 조금씩 마셔 보세요.
examples.en: When you feel nauseous, try sipping warm water little by little.

examples.ko: 어제부터 계속 메슥메슥한데 약을 먹어도 될까요?
examples.en: I've felt queasy since yesterday. Is it okay to take medicine?

explain: 토할 것 같고 속이 불편한 느낌이라 보통 '속이 메슥메슥하다'로 말해요. '메스껍다'도 같은 느낌으로 쓰고, '울렁거리다'는 속이 출렁이는 느낌이 더 커요. 멀미, 감기, 기름진 음식 뒤에 자주 나오는 표현이에요.

phrases.en: My stomach feels queasy, so I can't eat anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아서' 꼴로 속이 안 좋아서 생기는 결과를 이어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-아서' form links the queasy feeling to its result.

phrases.en: I ate greasy food, and now I feel nauseous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 느낌을 말하는 비슷한 말이고, 더 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for the same feeling, and it is more common.

phrases.en: After a long car ride, my stomach feels queasy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '메슥메슥하다'와 거의 같고 조금 더 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as '메슥메슥하다', just a shorter form.

explain_en: It describes the feeling of nearly throwing up and is usually said as '속이 메슥메슥하다' (my stomach feels queasy). '메스껍다' expresses the same feeling, while '울렁거리다' feels more like your insides are heaving. It fits motion sickness, colds, or after greasy food.

en: silk thread

examples.en: My grandmother embroidered a pretty pattern with silk thread.

examples.ko: 이 이불은 명주실로 짜서 아주 부드러워요.
examples.en: This blanket is woven from silk thread, so it is very soft.
The child's hair was as soft as silk thread.
Even single strands of silk thread become strong when gathered.
I bought a skein of silk thread at the shop.

examples.ko: 명주실이 너무 가늘어서 바늘에 꿰기 어려워요.
examples.en: The silk thread is so thin that it is hard to put through the needle.

explain: '명주'는 누에고치에서 나온 실로 짠 비단 종류의 천을 말하고, '명주실'은 그 실이에요. 머리카락이나 피부가 부드럽고 윤이 날 때 '명주실같이'라고 비유하기도 해요. 요즘 일상에서는 '실크'라는 말을 더 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 이 천은 명주실로 짠 거라서 가벼워요.
phrases.en: This fabric is woven from silk thread, so it is light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료를 말할 때 '-(으)로' 조사를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the particle -(으)로 to name the material.

phrases.en: My mother embroidered a handkerchief with silk thread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바느질이나 수놓기처럼 실을 쓰는 일과 함께 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears with needlework such as embroidery.

phrases.en: The baby's hair is soft like silk thread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 실이 아니라 부드럽고 윤이 나는 것을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use to describe something soft and glossy.

explain_en: '명주' is a silk-type cloth woven from thread from silkworm cocoons, and '명주실' is that thread. People sometimes compare soft, shiny hair or skin to it with '명주실같이'. In daily life today the word '실크' is used more often.

en: to be reddish; to be ruddy

examples.en: I walked in the cold, so my cheeks are ruddy.

examples.ko: 아이의 볼이 불그레해서 열이 있는지 만져 봤어요.
examples.en: The child's cheeks were flushed, so I touched them to check for a fever.
As the sun set, the sky was tinged a soft red.
I was so embarrassed that even my ears turned red.

examples.ko: 불그레한 얼굴로 들어온 동생이 웃고 있었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling came in with a flushed face, smiling.
Your skin is rosy after coming out of the bath.

explain: '빨갛다'가 선명한 빨강이라면 '불그레하다'는 살짝 붉은 정도예요. 추위, 부끄러움, 목욕 뒤의 볼·귀·피부나 노을처럼 은은한 붉은빛에 써요. 아주 짙은 붉은색에는 '새빨갛다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 술을 마셔서 얼굴이 불그레한 아저씨가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a man whose face is ruddy from drinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불그레한'으로 바꿔서 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form 불그레한 is used to describe a noun.

phrases.en: The evening sky glows faintly red.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불그레하다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A near synonym of 불그레하다 with almost the same meaning.

phrases.en: My face turned rosy because I was shy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불그레하다'보다 밝고 귀여운 붉은빛이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A brighter, cuter shade of red than 불그레하다.

explain_en: If '빨갛다' is a vivid red, '불그레하다' is only a slight red. It is used for faint redness, such as cheeks, ears, or skin after cold, embarrassment, or a bath, and for the soft glow of a sunset. For a very deep red, use '새빨갛다'.

en: to stick out; to pop out

examples.en: Your shirt is sticking out of your pants.
Some hair was sticking out of the hat.

examples.ko: 김밥 속 재료가 옆으로 삐져나와서 먹기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The filling is squeezing out of the side of the gimbap, so it's hard to eat.
If your feet stick out of the blanket, they get cold.
The bag is small, so things keep sticking out.

examples.ko: 빵 사이에서 크림이 삐져나오지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful so the cream doesn't squeeze out from between the bread.

explain: 틈이나 가장자리로 조금 튀어나온 모습에 써요. 옷, 머리카락, 속 재료처럼 안쪽에 있어야 할 것이 밖으로 나왔을 때 자연스러워요. '삐죽 나오다'와 비슷하지만, 안에 있던 것이 밀려 나온 느낌이 더 있어요.

phrases.example: 모자 밖으로 삐져나온 머리카락을 안으로 넣었어요.
phrases.en: I tucked the hair sticking out of my hat back inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 형태로 밖으로 나와 있는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun to describe something sticking out.

phrases.example: 속 재료가 삐져나오지 않게 김밥을 꼭 말아요.
phrases.en: Roll the gimbap tightly so the filling does not poke out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밖으로 나오지 않도록 조심할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used when taking care that something does not come out.
phrases.en_equiv: so that it does not stick out

phrases.example: 양말이 신발 밖으로 삐죽 나와 있어요.
phrases.en: The sock is sticking out of the shoe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝이 뾰족하게 조금 나온 모습이라 '삐져나오다'와 조금 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a tip poking out a little, which differs slightly from 삐져나오다.

explain_en: It describes something poking out slightly through a gap or edge, like clothes, hair or filling that should be inside. It is close to '삐죽 나오다', but it has more of a feel of something that was inside being pushed out.

en: to shave the head

examples.en: My husband shaved his head because it is summer.
Everyone shaves their head when they join the army.

examples.ko: 스님은 출가할 때 삭발하고 절에 들어가요.
examples.en: A monk shaves his head and enters the temple when he leaves home.

examples.ko: 삭발할 용기가 없어서 그냥 짧게 잘랐어요.
examples.en: I lacked the courage to shave it, so I just cut it short.
We bet that the losing team would shave their heads.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 영화 때문에 삭발한 모습으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: The actor appeared with a shaved head for the film.

explain: '삭발'의 '발(髮)'이 이미 머리털이라는 뜻이라 보통 '머리를 삭발하다'보다 '삭발하다'만 말해요. 입말에서는 '머리를 밀다'가 더 가볍게 들려요. 스스로 할 때도, 남이 해 줄 때도 같은 말을 써요.

phrases.en: My son shaved his head because it's summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삭발하다'보다 입말에서 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter, more casual way to say it in everyday speech than 삭발하다.

phrases.en: Please shave my head, sir.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 머리를 밀어 달라고 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking someone else to shave your head.

phrases.en: It's hot, so I want to shave my head.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삭발하다'에 '-고 싶다'를 붙여 내가 원하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds -고 싶다 to 삭발하다 to say what you want to do.
phrases.en_equiv: I want to shave my head

explain_en: The 발 (髮) in 삭발 already means hair, so people usually say just 삭발하다 rather than 머리를 삭발하다. In casual speech '머리를 밀다' sounds lighter. The same verb works whether you do it yourself or someone does it for you.

en: to point

examples.en: You shouldn't point at people.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 손가락질하며 사 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: The child pointed at the toy and asked me to buy it.
My friend shouted loudly while pointing over there.

examples.ko: 실수했다고 다들 저를 손가락질할까 봐 무서워요.
examples.en: I'm afraid everyone will point fingers at me for making a mistake.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 손가락질해도 저는 신경 안 써요.
examples.en: Even if people point fingers behind my back, I don't care.

examples.ko: 길에서 남을 손가락질하는 건 예의가 아니에요.
examples.en: Pointing at others on the street is not polite.

explain: 방향이나 물건을 알려 줄 때는 '가리키다'를 쓰고, '손가락질하다'는 손가락으로 사람을 가리키며 흉보거나 무시하는 느낌이 강해요. 예의 없는 행동으로 여겨서 사람에게는 잘 하지 않아요. '손가락질을 받다'처럼 비난받는다는 뜻으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: If you act like that, people will look down on you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 손가락으로 가리키지 않아도 사람들에게 비난이나 멸시를 받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means being blamed or looked down on by others, even if nobody literally points a finger.

explain_en: To simply show a direction or object, people use '가리키다'. '손가락질하다' often carries a feeling of blaming or looking down on someone, and pointing at a person is considered rude. It is also used as '손가락질을 받다' to mean being criticized.

en: to bow; to bend

examples.en: I greeted them with my head slightly bowed.
He lowered his head out of embarrassment.
I bent over and picked up the coin from the floor.
The ceiling is low, so you have to duck.
Why do you keep lowering your head?

examples.ko: 그는 고개를 수그린 채 말없이 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat silently with his head bowed.

explain: '숙이다'와 같은 뜻으로 고개, 허리, 몸 앞에 써요. 반대로 고개를 드는 건 '들다'나 '치켜들다'라고 하고, 저절로 숙여지는 건 '수그러지다'예요.

phrases.en: I bent over and tied my shoelaces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고개뿐 아니라 허리에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for the waist as well as the head.

phrases.en: The door is low, so please lower your head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 존댓말로 부탁하거나 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask or warn someone.

phrases.example: 그는 말없이 고개를 수그린 채 앉아 있었어요.
phrases.en: He sat there silently with his head bowed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 채'를 붙이면 그 상태가 계속된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -ㄴ 채 means the state continued.

explain_en: It means the same as '숙이다' and goes with head, waist or body. The opposite is '고개를 들다' (raise your head), and when something lowers on its own you say '수그러지다'.

en: to have a deep sleep; to get a sound sleep

examples.en: I slept soundly last night, so I felt refreshed this morning.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 차를 마시면 숙면하는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Drinking warm tea helps you sleep soundly.

examples.ko: 밤에 숙면하려면 낮에 커피를 줄여야 해요.
examples.en: To sleep soundly at night, you should cut back on coffee during the day.

examples.ko: 아기가 숙면해서 엄마도 쉴 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The baby slept soundly, so Mom could rest too.
On days I've slept soundly, the morning feels light.

examples.ko: 이 베개는 숙면할 수 있게 도와줘요.
examples.en: This pillow helps you sleep soundly.

explain: '자다'는 그냥 잠드는 일이고, '숙면하다'는 깊이 푹 잘 자는 것을 말해요. 말할 때는 '푹 자다'가 더 자연스럽고, 숙면하다는 건강 기사나 광고에서 자주 나와요. 명사 '숙면'은 '숙면을 취하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I slept well yesterday, so my body feels light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 이 표현이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the more natural expression in speech.

phrases.example: 운동을 하면 숙면을 취할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you exercise, you can get a deep sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '숙면'과 '취하다'를 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing of the noun 숙면 with 취하다.

phrases.example: 숙면하려면 자기 전에 휴대폰을 보지 마세요.
phrases.en: To sleep deeply, don't look at your phone before bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊이 자는 방법을 말할 때 '-려면'으로 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -려면 when talking about how to get deep sleep.

explain_en: 자다 just means to sleep, while 숙면하다 means sleeping deeply and well. In speech 푹 자다 sounds more natural, and 숙면하다 mostly appears in health articles and ads. The noun 숙면 is used as 숙면을 취하다.

en: wheeze; soft breathing sound

examples.en: The baby sleeps making soft breathing sounds.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸려서 숨 쉴 때마다 쌕쌕 소리가 나요.
examples.en: I have a cold, and there's a wheezing sound every time I breathe.

examples.ko: 고양이가 쌕쌕 숨 쉬면서 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is sleeping, breathing in light little breaths.
I ran here, so I'm breathing with a wheeze.
My younger sibling fell asleep snoring lightly.
I hear the child's wheezy breathing and I'm worried.

explain: 가늘고 가벼운 숨소리를 나타내요. 잠든 아기의 숨소리에도 쓰고, 감기나 숨이 찰 때 나는 쌕쌕거리는 소리에도 써요. 빠르고 힘찬 모양을 뜻하는 '쌩쌩'과 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: He ran over, panting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌕쌕'을 동사로 쓴 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 쌕쌕.

phrases.en: The baby is breathing with a soft sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨 쉬는 모습을 소리 흉내말로 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes breathing with a sound word.

phrases.en: I'm out of breath after climbing the stairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨이 가쁜 상태를 소리 흉내말 없이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says one is out of breath, without a sound word.

explain_en: It imitates a thin, light breathing sound. It is used for a sleeping baby's breath and also for the wheezy sound that comes with a cold or shortness of breath. Do not confuse it with '쌩쌩', which means fast and full of energy.

en: feeling of a foreign body; foreign sensation

examples.en: My eye felt like something was in it, so I kept rubbing it.
When you first wear braces, they feel foreign in your mouth.

examples.ko: 렌즈를 처음 끼면 이물감 때문에 불편해요.
examples.en: When you first put in contact lenses, the foreign feeling is uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 목에 이물감이 계속 남아서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: The feeling of something stuck in my throat stayed, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 이 화장품은 피부에 바르면 이물감이 없어요.
examples.en: This cosmetic doesn't feel heavy or foreign when applied to the skin.

examples.ko: 이물감이 심하면 의사에게 꼭 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: If the foreign feeling is strong, please be sure to tell the doctor.

explain: 눈, 목, 입안, 피부에 무언가 낀 것처럼 불편한 느낌을 말해요. 렌즈, 교정기, 화장품, 병원 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '이질감'은 서로 달라서 어울리지 않는 느낌이라 사람이나 분위기에도 쓰지만, 이물감은 몸에서 느끼는 감각에 써요.

phrases.en: I feel something foreign in my eye every time I blink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기도 모르게 불편함이 느껴진다는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests discomfort that one notices without trying.

phrases.en: These lenses have no foreign feeling, so they're comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품이 편하다고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say a product is comfortable.

phrases.example: 새 틀니에 이물감을 느끼는 사람이 많아요.
phrases.en: Many people feel a foreign sensation with new dentures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 직접 느낀다는 점을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses that the person is experiencing it directly.

explain_en: It refers to the uncomfortable sensation of something being stuck in your eye, throat, mouth or skin. It often appears in talk about lenses, braces, cosmetics and hospitals. '이질감' is the awkward feeling of things not fitting together and can be used for people or atmosphere, while '이물감' is for a physical sensation in the body.

en: calf

examples.en: After walking a long time, my calves hurt.
I got a cramp in my calf while sleeping.
After I rubbed my calf, it loosened up a bit.
My calf muscles are well developed.
I got a calf massage after the marathon.
Calves get firm quickly when you exercise.

explain: '종아리'와 비슷하지만 '장딴지'는 종아리 뒤쪽 불룩한 근육 부분을 가리켜요. 일상 대화에서는 '종아리'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I stood for a long time, and my calves feel tight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '장딴지'보다 훨씬 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used much more often in daily speech than '장딴지'.

phrases.en: After exercising, my calves got thicker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 근육이 붙었거나 다리 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used about muscle or the shape of the legs.

phrases.en: I massaged my sore calf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피로를 풀려고 다리를 손으로 누를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when rubbing the leg to relieve fatigue.

explain_en: It is close to '종아리' (lower leg), but 장딴지 points to the bulging muscle on the back of the lower leg. In daily conversation people also often just say '종아리'.

en: leggings; tight-fitting pants

examples.en: Wearing leggings with a long T-shirt is comfortable.
Tight pants are good to wear when exercising.
I bought a new pair of leggings yesterday.
These leggings are so tight that sitting is uncomfortable.
In winter I wear tights under my skirt.

examples.ko: 요즘은 쫄바지 대신 통 넓은 바지가 유행이에요.
examples.en: These days wide-leg pants are in fashion instead of skinny ones.

explain: 몸에 딱 붙는 바지를 편하게 부르는 입말이에요. 패션이나 운동복 이야기에서는 '레깅스'라는 말도 많이 써요. 쫄쫄 붙는 느낌이라 조금 가볍고 장난스러운 말투예요.

phrases.en: I often wear leggings when I exercise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쫄바지'보다 일반적이고 단정한 말이에요. 패션이나 운동복 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More standard and neutral than '쫄바지', used when talking about fashion or sportswear.

phrases.en: In winter I wear leggings under my skirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 이름과 가장 자주 쓰는 동사 '입다'를 함께 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The clothing name used with the most common verb, '입다'.

phrases.en: They're tight pants, so they're a little uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쫄바지'를 풀어서 설명하는 말이에요. 몸에 꼭 맞는 바지를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A way to explain '쫄바지' in plain words: pants that fit tightly on the body.

explain_en: This is a casual spoken word for pants that cling to the body. In talk about fashion or sportswear, people also use the word '레깅스'. It sounds a little light and playful.

en: to come up short

examples.ko: 요즘 잠을 못 자서 몸이 축나요.
examples.en: I can't sleep these days, so my health is wearing down.

examples.ko: 밤샘 작업이 계속되면 건강이 축나기 마련이에요.
examples.en: If all-nighters continue, your health is bound to suffer.

examples.ko: 쌀 한 말이라고 했는데 재 보니 축났어요.
examples.en: They said it was one mal of rice, but when I weighed it, it was short.
My savings shrink every month, and I'm worried.

examples.ko: 이렇게 일만 하다가는 몸이 축날 거예요.
examples.en: If you keep working like this, your body will wear out.
After all that emotional stress, your face looks worn.

explain: '몸이 축나다', '건강이 축나다'처럼 피로나 고생으로 몸이 상하고 약해질 때 가장 많이 써요. 양이나 돈이 줄어 모자랄 때도 쓰는데, 누군가 일부러 줄이면 '축내다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 일이 많아서 건강이 축날까 봐 걱정돼요.
phrases.en: I worry my health will suffer because of too much work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강이 나빠지는 상황에 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used when health declines.

phrases.example: 밤을 새웠더니 몸이 축난 것 같아요.
phrases.en: After staying up all night, I feel worn out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피곤하거나 고생해서 몸이 약해졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the body is worn down by tiredness or hardship.

phrases.example: 그는 일도 안 하고 밥만 축내요.
phrases.en: He doesn't work and just eats up the food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 줄어드는 '축나다'와 달리 누군가 원인이 되어 양을 줄일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 축나다, used when someone causes something to shrink.

explain_en: It is most often used as '몸이 축나다' or '건강이 축나다' when fatigue or hardship wears the body down. It also fits amounts or money that shrink and fall short. When someone reduces something, the paired word is '축내다'.

en: to be congested; to be bloodshot

examples.en: I played games all night, so my eyes are bloodshot.
My eyes turned red and bloodshot, so I went to the hospital.
Your eyes are bloodshot, maybe from crying.

examples.ko: 렌즈를 오래 끼면 눈이 충혈되기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you wear contact lenses for a long time, your eyes easily get bloodshot.
Everyone was worried when I came to work with bloodshot eyes.
I put in eye drops so my eyes wouldn't get bloodshot.

explain: '눈이 충혈되다'처럼 대부분 눈에 대해 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '눈이 빨개지다', '눈에 핏발이 서다'라고도 해요. 피곤하거나 울었거나 눈에 병이 났을 때 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: My eyes turned red because I cried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충혈되다보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 충혈되다 and common in daily conversation.

phrases.example: 잠을 못 자서 눈에 핏발이 섰어요.
phrases.en: My eyes got bloodshot because I couldn't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 붉은 실핏줄이 보일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when red blood vessels show in the eyes.

phrases.en: I went to work with bloodshot eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form that describes the noun that follows.

explain_en: Most often it is used for eyes, as in '눈이 충혈되다'. In daily talk people also say '눈이 빨개지다' or '눈에 핏발이 서다'. It describes eyes after tiredness, crying or an eye infection.

en: flat foot

examples.ko: 저는 평발이라서 오래 걸으면 발이 아파요.
examples.en: I have flat feet, so my feet hurt when I walk for a long time.

examples.ko: 평발은 운동화를 신을 때 깔창이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: For flat feet, an insole helps when you wear sneakers.
I had the hospital check whether my child has flat feet.

examples.ko: 평발인 사람은 신발을 고를 때 신경 써야 해요.
examples.en: People with flat feet need to be careful when choosing shoes.
My younger sibling has flat feet but runs well.
I'm looking for shoes that suit flat feet.

explain: 발바닥이 평평한 발을 말하고, 보통 '평발이다', '평발이라서'처럼 자기 몸 이야기를 할 때 많이 써요. 신발 가게나 병원에서 자주 듣는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 저는 평발이라서 오래 걷는 게 힘들어요.
phrases.en: I have flat feet, so walking for a long time is hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 몸 상태를 말할 때 '평발이다'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state your own physical condition.

phrases.en: It hurts less since I put in flat-foot insoles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발 가게에서 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often heard in shoe stores.

phrases.example: 평발인 사람은 오래 서 있으면 피곤해요.
phrases.en: People with flat feet get tired when standing for long.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-인'을 붙여 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-인' ending modifies the noun 'person'.

explain_en: It refers to feet with flat soles and is usually used when talking about one's own body, as in '평발이다' or '평발이라서'. You often hear it in shoe shops and at the doctor's.

en: to be chubby; to be plump; to be round

examples.ko: 아기 볼이 포동포동해서 자꾸 만지고 싶어요.
examples.en: The baby's cheeks are so chubby that I keep wanting to touch them.
The puppy's plump little paws are so cute.

examples.ko: 석 달 된 조카가 포동포동하게 살이 올랐어요.
examples.en: My three-month-old nephew has put on nice chubby weight.

examples.ko: 젖살이 포동포동 오른 아이 얼굴이 사랑스러워요.
examples.en: The child's face, with its chubby baby fat, is adorable.
The baby's arms are plump and soft.

examples.ko: 어릴 적 사진 속 저는 포동포동했어요.
examples.en: In my childhood photos, I was chubby.

explain: '통통하다'와 비슷하지만 '포동포동하다'는 아기나 작은 동물처럼 귀엽고 말랑해 보이는 통통함에 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 귀엽게 놀리는 말처럼 들릴 수 있어서 조심하는 게 좋아요. '포동포동'은 부사로도 써요.

phrases.en: The baby's chubby cheeks are so cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 '-한'으로 바꿔 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changes to '-한' when modifying a noun.

phrases.en: The baby ate well and became chubby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 통통하게 변하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes gradually becoming plump.

phrases.en: The puppy has plumped up nicely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '포동포동'을 써서 귀엽게 살이 찐 모습을 그려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form paints a cute picture of gaining weight.

explain_en: It is similar to '통통하다' but is used for a cute, soft-looking plumpness, like that of babies or small animals. Said about adults, it can sound like affectionate teasing, so be careful. '포동포동' is also used as an adverb.

en: feeling full

examples.en: Foods that keep you full for a long time are good for dieting.

examples.ko: 너무 빨리 먹으면 포만감을 느끼기 어려워요.
examples.en: If you eat too fast, it's hard to feel full.

examples.ko: 이 빵은 포만감이 커서 한 개면 충분해요.
examples.en: This bread is so filling that one is enough.
If you drink a lot of water, you also feel full.

examples.ko: 포만감은 먹은 뒤 조금 지나서야 느껴져요.
examples.en: The feeling of fullness comes only a little while after eating.
I'm so full that I can't eat dessert.

explain: '배부르다'가 일상에서 쓰는 말이라면, '포만감'은 배부른 느낌 자체를 설명할 때 써서 다이어트, 식사, 건강 이야기에 많이 나와요. '포만감이 들다/느끼다/오래가다'처럼 쓰고, 반대는 '허기'예요.

phrases.en: I feel full when I drink water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배부른 느낌이 생기는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the feeling of fullness arising.

phrases.en: Oats make you feel full, so they're good for breakfast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 배부른 느낌을 만들어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a food creates a full feeling.
phrases.en_equiv: to give a feeling of fullness

phrases.example: 이 빵은 양이 적어도 포만감이 커요.
phrases.en: This bread is small, but it's very filling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹은 뒤에 배부른 정도가 크다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the sense of fullness after eating is strong.

explain_en: While '배부르다' is the everyday word, '포만감' names the feeling of fullness itself and appears a lot in talk about diets, meals and health. It is used as '포만감이 들다/느끼다/오래가다', and the opposite idea is '허기' (hunger).

en: to come loose; to fit loosely

examples.en: The pants are so big that the waist is loose.
I must have lost weight, because my ring keeps feeling loose.

examples.ko: 신발이 헐렁거려서 오래 걸으면 발이 아파요.
examples.en: The shoes fit loosely, so my feet hurt when I walk for long.

examples.ko: 의자 다리가 헐렁거리고 삐걱거려서 앉기 무서워요.
examples.en: The chair leg is wobbly and creaky, so I'm scared to sit on it.

examples.ko: 헐렁거리는 옷을 입으면 편하지만 멋은 없어요.
examples.en: Loose clothes are comfortable, but they don't look stylish.

examples.ko: 이 바지는 허리가 헐렁거리지 않고 몸에 잘 맞아요.
examples.en: The waist of these pants isn't loose, and they fit well.

explain: '헐렁하다'는 옷이 몸에 비해 크다는 상태를 말하고, '헐렁거리다'는 헐거워서 흔들리는 느낌까지 있어요. 옷이 큰 것만 말할 때는 '헐렁하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 반대로 꼭 끼면 '꽉 끼다', 딱 맞으면 '딱 맞다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This T-shirt is loose, so it's comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이 크다는 상태만 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural when you only mean that clothes are big on you.

phrases.en: I like wearing loose clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 크게 입는 취향을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a preference for wearing clothes loose.

phrases.en: I lost weight, so my clothes became loose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 변해서 옷이 커진 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your body changes and clothes feel big.

explain_en: '헐렁하다' just describes clothes being too big, while '헐렁거리다' also gives the feeling of something loose and wobbling. To say only that clothes are big, '헐렁하다' sounds more natural. The opposites are '꽉 끼다' (fit too tight) and '딱 맞다' (fit just right).

en: to burn; to glow; to flush

examples.en: My face suddenly felt hot, so I looked in the mirror.
I made a mistake during my presentation and even my ears burned.

examples.ko: 햇볕에 탄 등이 아직도 화끈거리는데 어떡하죠?
examples.en: My sunburned back still stings and burns. What should I do?
I ate spicy food and now my mouth is burning.
The knee I fell on started to burn and hurt.

examples.ko: 찬물로 씻었더니 화끈거리던 얼굴이 좀 나아졌어요.
examples.en: After washing with cold water, my burning face felt a bit better.

explain: 열이 나거나 따갑거나 부끄러울 때 몸의 한 부분이 뜨겁게 느껴지는 것을 말해요. '화끈하다'는 성격이 시원시원하다는 뜻으로도 쓰지만, '화끈거리다'는 몸의 느낌에 써요. 부끄러울 때는 '얼굴이 화끈거리다'가 가장 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 아까 한 말이 생각나서 얼굴이 화끈거려요.
phrases.en: I remembered what I said earlier and my face is burning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 열이 나지 않아도 창피하거나 부끄러울 때 써요. 실수한 일을 떠올릴 때 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used even when there is no real heat, to say you feel ashamed or embarrassed. People say it often when recalling a mistake.

explain_en: It describes a body part feeling hot from heat, stinging or embarrassment. '화끈하다' can also mean someone is bold and straightforward, but '화끈거리다' is about physical sensation. When you are embarrassed, '얼굴이 화끈거리다' is the most natural phrase.
